newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALL NEWSPAPERS

Indian investigators released the names of five people they said had received payments from Swedish arms manufacturer Bofors in connection with a $1.3 billion artillery contract in 1986. A statement from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said a first set of documents had been received from Swiss authorities. A CBI spokesman said the investigating agency would try to determine the nature of the payments.
The Economic Times
INDIAN NORMS STRICT BUT APPLICATION TARDY

Poor implementation by a slow bureaucracy of otherwise strong norms and laws were hindering investment, the U.S. Trade Representative's (USTR) National Trade Estimate (NTE) on India for 1996 said. It said though norms such as those on food safety were more stringent than international norms, they were ineffective due to poor enforcement. The NTE report said opponents of foreign investment tried to apply these laws selectively to U.S. firms which recently opened operations in India. But it noted that such attempts did not withstand judicial scrutiny. The USTR was confident that India was seeking to harmonise national norms with international norms.
Financial Express
STATE BANK, GE CAPITAL MAY TIE UP FOR CREDIT CARDS

State Bank of India (SBI) was likely to tie up with GE Capital for its proposed one billion rupee credit card subsidiary. Banking sources said GE Capital had made detailed presentations before SBI over the technical expertise it could offer for setting up the subsidiary and was now negotiating with the bank over the equity stake. Sources further disclosed that SBI also had discussions with two other foreign firms including American Express and Capital One of the United States.
COAL PRICE, DISTRIBUTION DECONTROLLED

The government approved a new coal policy, lifting price and distribution controls from practically all grades of coal. It also decided to locate new power plants at the pitheads and increase use of lignite in power generation. While exploration and mining in the private sector was subject to legislative amendments, coal prices and distribution could be decontrolled almost at once.
GLOBAL TENDERS SOON FOR PORT PROJECTS

The government identified 26 projects in the port sector with an estimated cost of 200 billion rupees for which global tenders were to be invited soon. Surface Transport Ministry sources said the government would encourage innovative proposals put forward by private companies. A committee would be set up to deal with such offers. Ports have been authorised to lease out existing assets to private investors on the condition that such leasing resulted in upgradation of facilities or fresh investment leading to higher productivity.
Business Standard
FIXED TO-CELLULAR TARIFF PROPOSAL TO BE REVIEWED

A breakthrough in the impasse between cellular operators and the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), over the latter's move to hike tariffs for calls made from fixed line phones to cellular subscribers, appeared in sight. The firms were assured of a detailed study into the matter by the Communications Minister. The assurance came after the Delhi High Court rejected an interim stay plea by the Cellular Operators Association of India against the DoT move. The minister's promise that the matter would be referred to the Telecom Regulatory Authority, if necessary, was welcomed by the cellular companies.
SUMITOMO TO ENTER POWER, TELECOM

Japanese conglomerate Sumitomo Corporation will launch a fully-owned Indian subsidiary on April 1. The company, Sumitomo Corporation India Ltd, will be launched with approximately $4 million in initial share capital. It will focus on investments in the power, telecommunications, automobile, chemicals, agriculture and export sectors. Sumitomo Bank will also set up its first branch in Bombay around the same time, while Summit Usha Martin Finance, one of Sumitomo's joint ventures in India, was set to emerge as the financier for future projects taken up by Sumitomo Corporation.
COAL MINING BY PRIVATE FIRMS ALLOWED

The government has decided to allow local private companies to enter into coal and lignite mining. They would be permitted to have foreign equity partners subject to clearance from the government. A bill would be moved in parliament to amend the current norms to allow any Indian company to mine coal and lignite for captive consumption and also for sale.
The Observer
CASTROL NET DOWN TO 945.3 MLN RUPEES

Castrol India, the leading specialist lubricant company in the country, posted higher gross turnover at 8.88 billion rupees for the year ending December 31, 1996. This was against 7.14 billion rupees for the previous year. However, net profit went down by 8.27 percent to 945.3 million rupees from 1.03 billion in the previous year.
Business Line
ICICI SHARES IN SCICI TO BE EXTINGUISHED

Shares held by ICICI in SCICI, aggregating 20 percent of the company, would now be extinguished. This would pave the way for a reduced capital base for the merged entity. The ICICI board decided to adopt this method instead of transferring the shares to a trust and then offering them to shareholders and the public. The equity base of the merged entity would be 4.76 billion rupees and shareholders of both the companies approved the merger proposal. By extinguishing these shares, the capital of the merged entity would be lower, resulting in a higher earnings per share ratio.
